  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that
seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments
received after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public re
of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
 comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments
received after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public re
of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities
of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to
observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by
contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310 -412-5280, FAX at 310 -412-5533, One
Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to
athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

Inglewood, California
  October 3, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  October 3, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel
  present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager/Acting Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  September 28, 2023, in the amount of $9,092,753.14, and dated September 28, 2023, in
  the amount of $560,752.78 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members Gray,
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman/ Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

125  AMENDMENT ONE TO AGREEMENT NO. 22-221 APPROVED – BURKE,
  WILLIAMS & SORENSEN, LLP; PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING INVOICES
  AUTHORIZED – BURKE, WILLIAMS & SORENSEN, LLP; SPECIAL
  COUNSEL’S ENGAGEMENT AUTHORIZED – RELOCATION SERVICES AND
  LITIGATION SUPPORT RELATED TO THE INGLEWOOD BASKETBALL
  ENTERTAINMENT CENTER (IBEC).  Staff report dated October 3, 2023, was
  presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment One
  to Agreement No. 22-221 with Burke, Williams & Sorensen, LLP (“Special Counsel”) for
  broad ranging legal advice, guidance, and representation in an additional amount not to
  exceed One Million Dollars ($1,000,000), for a total amount not to exceed One Million Five
  Hundred Dollars ($1,500,000) for Agreement No. 22-221.
 October 3, 2023

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment One to Agreement No. 22-221; 2)
  Authorize payment of outstanding invoices in an amount not to exceed One-hundred and
  fifty thousand dollars ($150,000); and 3) Authorize Special Counsel’s engagement of Del
  Richards & Associates, Inc. for relocation services and litigation support related to the
  Inglewood Basketball Entertainment Center (IBEC). The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  RESOLUTION NO. 24-01 ADOPTED - AUTHORIZING ACCEPTANCE OF
  FISCAL YEAR 2023-2023 ALCOHOL POLICING PARTNERSHIP GRANT AND
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-2023 BUDGET. Staff report dated October 3,
  2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution
  authorizing acceptance of the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Alcohol Policing Partnership grant, in
  the amount of $74,967, and amending the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Budget to include said
  funds.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 24-01 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE ACCEPTANCE OF GRANT FUNDS
  FROM THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF ALCOHOLIC
  BEVERAGE CONTROL IN THE AMOUNT OF $74,967

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-265 APPROVED – HF&H
  CONSULTANTS, LLC (HF&H). Staff report dated October 3, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment No. 2 to
  Agreement No. 20-265 with HF&H Consultants, LLC (HF&H) for ongoing solid waste
  monitoring consulting services for an additional three years (beginning December 1, 2023,
  to November 30, 2026), in an amount not to exceed $299,000, with a ten (10) percent
  contingency compensation allowance for a total amount not to exceed $328,900.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 20-265. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 24-002 APPROVED – VOLTAIRE ENGINEERING, INC.;
  PROJECT CONTINGENCY APPROVED; RESOLUTION NO. 24-02 ADOPTED -
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET. Staff report dated October 3,
  2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve an
  agreement with Voltaire Engineering, Inc., for the Vincent Park Decomposed Granite
  Project, per Bid No. CB-23-16.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 24-002 in an amount not to
  exceed $190,800; 2) Approve a ten percent (10%) project contingency in an amount not to
  exceed $19,080 for a total project budget amount not to exceed $209,880; and 3) Adopt
  Resolution No. 24-02 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET TO
  FUND THE VINCENT PARK DECOMPOSED GRANITE PROJECT

  2
 October 3, 2023

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-003 APPROVED –
  TRIANGLE DECON SERVICES, INC; CITY-CONTROLLED CONTINGENCY
  APPROVED; RESOLUTION NO. 24-03 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET. Staff report dated October 3, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve an
  agreement with Triangle Decon Services, Inc., for the Renovations to District Four
  Community Center Project, per Bid No. RFB-0164.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award a contract and approve Agreement No. 24-003 in
  an amount not to exceed $98,060.40; 2) Approve a City-controlled contingency of twenty
  percent (20%) or $19,612.08 for a total amount not to exceed $117,672.48; and 3) Adopt
  Resolution No. 24-03 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET TO FUND
  THE RENOVATIONS TO DISTRICT FOUR’S COMMUNITY CENTER

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

173  ORDINANCE NO. 24-01 INTRODUCED – SALARY ORDINANCE FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2023-2024. Staff report dated October 3, 2023, was presented recommending that
  the Mayor and Council Members introduce the attached Salary Ordinance for Fiscal Year
  2023-2024.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 24-01 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  ESTABLISHING PAY RANGE ASSIGNMENT AND CONDITIONS OF
  EMPLOYMENT FOR THE VARIOUS OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES AND
  POSITIONS IN THE SERVICE OF THE CITY FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024;
  INCLUDING THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR (ITC) GRANT
  FUNDED TRANSITIONAL APPOITMENTS AND REPEALING ALL PREVIOUS
  ORDINANCES OF THE CITY IN CONFLICT OR AT  VARIANCE HEREWITH;
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,
  DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  was introduced by Council Member Morales.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson notified residents about the
  Primary Election on March 5, 2024. She stated that her office was working with the Los
  Angeles Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk’s Office to utilize City Hall as a centralized
  polling location. She also notified residents about sample ballots mailed out on January 5,
  2024, and vote-by-mail ballots mailed by February 5, 2024. Additionally, she stated that
  she would bring more information as the time draws near. Finally, she pointed out that
  October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and
  Attention Deficit Hypertension Awareness Month.

126  MONTHLY TREASURER’S REPORT. Staff report dated October 3, 2023, was
  presented submitting the Monthly Treasurer’s Report for the month ending August 31, 2023.
  Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.
  3
 October 3, 2023

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning being racially profiled by another resident.
  He stated that the resident broke the windows out of his building and harassed his fiancée
  and staff members. He mentioned that a future press conference would address this issue
  and that he was also working with a detective to investigate this. Additionally, the
  speaker added that the resident was out of control, and he knew nothing about him until
  he moved into the building. He also mentioned the names of city employees he had
  contacted to help. Furthermore, he added that a KKK member gave him a coin and told
  him they no longer wanted him in the building and had been trying to force him out for two
  years. Finally, he reiterated his attempts to communicate with City of Inglewood representatives
  but felt he didn’t receive any assistance resolving this matter.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) asked the Mayor about Downey and Warren playing football at
  the SoFi Stadium instead of Hawthorne High School and Inglewood High School.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the honor of Edmond Hamilton, Sr., at the hour of 2:26 p.m.

  Approved this ___ day of _________, 2023.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
